question: If the Earth shrinks such that its density becomes $8$ times the present value, then the new duration of the day in hours will be
solution:
The mass stays the same, so $8$ times the density means $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the volume, i.e. half the radius.

With no external torque, $I\omega$ is constant and $I \propto R^2$, so $\omega$ becomes $4$ times and the day becomes $\dfrac{24}{4} = 6$ hours.
